common.style_usage: Stardew Valley building pixel art: palette, outline weight, how the roofs are shaded in rows of tiles or shingles with light ridges, dark gable edges and deep shadow under the eaves, and the high top-down front camera where the roof fills over half the building
common.reference_usage: camera, silhouette and roof planes: the lighter roof colour is roof facing up toward the viewer, the darker is roof facing forward, the darkest band is the shadow under the eaves; keep this outline, these openings, and the roof taking more than half the height

studio_large_r1.description: The largest of the Vale's old artists' studios in Stardew Valley pixel art, long empty but a proper, handsome building worth reopening: a tall grey-green slate front-gabled roof with a big slanted north-light skylight of glass panes (a few cracked), pale dressed-stone walls with moss at the base, a lower side wing on the right with a mossy wooden-shingle roof and its own small window, a wide many-paned studio window on the front with one pane boarded, a blank painted sign board above an ordinary single wooden door the size of a person (the same size as a Stardew Valley house door, not taller than the windows' tops), ivy on one corner. STRICTLY FRONT-FACING like every Stardew Valley building: the front wall seen square-on and flat, not turned or rotated, no three-quarter or isometric angle; the roof seen from above and in front, its ridge running back away from the viewer, the two roof planes filling about 60% of the height. Building only, nothing around it, no ground, no text, transparent background. The whole building fits inside the picture with clear space above the roof's ridge: draw the complete roof, nothing cut off.
